articles.author: Claudia Grisales
articles.description: Democrats won by making inroads in several states where they have long struggled, boosted by a challenging political environment for the GOP dominated by voter frustration over high prices.
articles.title: Democrats win the Senate, setting up divided government for remainder of Trump's term

articles.author: Natalie Krebs
articles.description: Democrat Josh Turek has defeated Sen. Ashley Hinson in Iowa, according to a race call by the Associated Press.
articles.title: Democrat Josh Turek wins the Senate seat in Iowa

articles.author: Maayan Silver
articles.description: Democrat David Crowley defeated Republican Congressman Tom Tiffany in a campaign that focused on "lowering costs for working families" and bringing more jobs to Wisconsin.
articles.title: Democrat David Crowley will be Wisconsin's first Black governor

articles.author: Jason Rosenbaum
articles.description: Missouri voters defeated a measure that would have banned abortion just two years after voters legalized abortion in another vote. Voters in Missouri legalized abortion two years ago but this time the abortion ban was coupled with a ban on transgender treatment for minors. Opponents said it was misleading.
articles.title: Missourians reject ballot proposal that would have re-imposed an abortion ban

articles.author: Blaise Gainey
articles.description: Hinojosa, an Austin state representative, is set to be the state's first Democratic governor since 1995 and will be the state's first Latina governor.
articles.title: Democrat Gina Hinojosa wins race for Texas governor, ousting Greg Abbott

articles.author: Sheila Brummer
articles.description: Democratic State Auditor Rob Sand stressed affordability and often talked about how his Christian faith guides him.
articles.title: Democrat Rob Sand wins Iowa governor's race, ending GOP control of the office

articles.author: Benjamin Swasey
articles.description: Missouri voters have denied a Republican-backed congressional map that wound its way through the courts before ultimately ending up on the state's ballot.
articles.title: Missouri voters turn down a Republican-backed congressional map

articles.author: Karen Kasler
articles.description: Democratic former U.S. Sen. Sherrod Brown has won back a seat on Capitol Hill, defeating incumbent Republican Sen. Jon Husted after a close and expensive battle, according to a race call by the Associated Press.
articles.title: Democrat Sherrod Brown wins Ohio Senate race

articles.author: Andrew Schneider
articles.description: Democrat James Talarico has won the Senate seat in Texas, according to a race call by the Associated Press.
articles.title: Democrat James Talarico wins Texas Senate seat

articles.author: Sarah Donaldson
articles.description: Democrat Amy Acton beat biotech entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy, a Republican backed by President Trump, in a race marked in the final weeks by a Ramaswamy attack ad that drew national criticism.
articles.title: Ohio elects Amy Acton first woman governor

articles.author: Shrai Popat and Cecilia Nowell (now); Lucy Campbell (earlier)
articles.description:
Democrats flip seats in Texas, Iowa, Kansas, North Carolina, South Carolina and Ohio; Trump says he will accept results in a dire night for Republicans

Track live results from all 50 states

Democrats win control of Senate as US voters reject Trump’s agenda

As we bring you the latest from around the country, Donald Trump is certainly paying attention. From the White House, the president said that he was tuning into coverage on Fox News.
“I can’t stand Jessica Tarlov’s voice,” Trump said of the Democratic strategist and Fox News contributor in a post on Truth Social. The president called Tarlov “DUMB AS A ROCK”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US midterm elections 2026 live updates: Democrats win Senate control and edge toward House victory

articles.author: Lauren Gambino
articles.description:
Hinojosa wins momentous victory, shatters Republican grip on key office and will become state’s first Latina governor

US midterm elections – live updates

Track live results from all 50 states

In a stunning political upset that would have seemed improbable only a few weeks ago, Democrat Gina Hinojosa has defeated three-term governor Greg Abbott on Tuesday, shattering the Republican grip on the highest and most powerful executive office in Texas.
Hinojosa’s historic victory – she will be the state’s first ever Latina governor – ended Abbott’s bid for an unprecedented fourth term, and delivered Democrats their most consequential victory in the state in a generation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeats Texas governor Greg Abbott in stunning upset

articles.author: Shrai Popat and Robert Tait
articles.description:
Democratic nominee toppled the five-term Republican incumbent in one of the most hard-fought midterm contests

US midterm elections – live updates

Track live results from all 50 states

Tell us: what do you want to know about the midterm election results?

The Democrat Troy Jackson has won Maine’s US Senate race, toppling five-term Republican incumbent Susan Collins in one of the biggest upsets of the 2026 midterms.
Jackson, 58, unseated Collins – who has been in the Senate since 1997 – in a closely fought, and often rancorous, race characterized by mutual accusations of corruption and clashes over living costs in the predominantly rural state.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrat Troy Jackson defeats Susan Collins to win Maine US Senate seat in blow to Republicans

articles.author: Lois Beckett and Chris Stein
articles.description:
Sand, auditor for state with strong Trump support, defeats Maha-backed Republican Zach Lahn as Democrats win big

US midterms 2026 live – latest updates

Track live results from all 50 states

Democrat Rob Sand has been elected governor of Iowa, the Associated Press projects, a milestone as his party seeks to rebuild its political standing in the midwestern state.
Sand, the state auditor who is the sole Democrat holding statewide office in Iowa, triumphed over Republican Zach Lahn, a political newcomer backed by Robert F Kennedy Jr’s “Make America healthy again” movement.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrat Rob Sand wins Iowa’s gubernatorial race as party plans rebuild

articles.author: Antonio Voce, Seán Clarke, Ed Gargan, Anna Leach and Ashley Kirk
articles.description:
Latest results suggest the Democrats are almost certain to win a House majority, having already seized control of the Senate. Find live updating results in full here

US midterm elections – live updates

The US legislature, Congress, has two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US midterm elections 2026: live results from Senate, House and governor races in all 50 states

articles.author: Matthew Weaver
articles.description:
Exclusive: Schools minister launches new Ukrainian GCSE and says she is sorry students were pushed to study Russian in its absence
The UK has apologised to Ukrainian child refugees who were told to study Russian in English schools, as it launched funding for a new GCSE in Ukrainian.
Ukrainian children who were forced to seek refuge in the UK after Vladimir Putin’s invasion in 2022 say it was “insulting” that their teachers suggested they study Russian in the absence of a GCSE in Ukrainian.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK apologises to Ukrainian child refugees who were told to study Russian

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
Report led by Peter Garrett and former defence chief Adm Chris Barrie says agreement should be suspended and calls for royal commission

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

A public inquiry into the $368bn Aukus nuclear submarine agreement has called the plan “the worst, riskiest and most costly defence decision ever made by an Australian government”, urging its immediate termination.
Former Labor MP and Midnight Oil frontman Peter Garrett and former chief of defence Adm Chris Barrie led the inquiry dominated by critics of the deal with the UK and US, recommending the suspension of plans for new bases and for a royal commission to be held into the agreement signed by the former Morrison government.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Aukus is ‘worst, riskiest and most costly’ Australian defence decision ever, public inquiry into submarine deal says

articles.author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
articles.description:
Police also allege Torquay man was attacked with a ‘blunt weapon’ rather than a baseball bat as originally reported

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An alleged attack on a One Nation supporter is not believed to have been politically motivated, Victoria police say, clarifying that a “blunt weapon” was allegedly used rather than a baseball bat as originally reported.
On Tuesday, police confirmed they arrested a 37-year-old Hampton Park man and a 14-year-old boy over the alleged attack on a 60-year-old man outside his Torquay home on Sunday night.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alleged attack on One Nation supporter not believed to be politically motivated, Victoria police say

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts
The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure.
The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party. However, polls show it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the last municipal elections in 2021 and 40.2% in 2024’s national elections.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ANC faces anger over poor services as South Africans vote in local elections

articles.author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Community and Public Sector Union denounces ‘privatisation by stealth’, joining growing number of unions turning on Carroll government

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victoria’s public servants union says it will not support Labor at this month’s state election, condemning the government for cutting public service jobs while spending $1.2bn on consultants.
The Community and Public Sector Union (CPSU) will announce the decision on Wednesday, joining several other unions that have refused to back Labor or are actively campaigning against the government ahead of the 28 November poll.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Public service union refuses to back Labor at Victorian election, condemning job cuts and $1.2bn consultant spend

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Rideshare company unsuccessfully argued it didn’t employ workers and claimed money paid was not wages under NSW law
The rideshare behemoth Uber has suffered a bruising loss in Australia’s high court that will cost it more than $80m in unpaid taxes.
The court on Wednesday dismissed Uber’s claim it was not liable to pay payroll tax in New South Wales after it argued that it does not employ drivers and claimed that money paid to its drivers were not wages under state law.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Uber pays its drivers ‘wages’ and is liable for $81m payroll tax bill, Australia’s high court rules

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Growing number of countries are resisting Russia’s reintegration into international hockey after a sports court lifted a ban on competition
Canada has joined a coalition of countries refusing to play ⁠ice ​hockey teams from Russia, with prime minister Mark Carney saying Russian skaters will not be able to compete in ⁠a world junior championship next month due to the war in Ukraine.
“While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified, horrific ‌war in Ukraine, as long as that’s going on, there will be none of ​those athletes competing for their countries in Canada,” Carney told reporters on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada joins coalition refusing to play ice hockey against Russia over Ukraine war

articles.author: Jonathan Barrett Business editor
articles.description:
Chief executive Melanie Perkins describes job cuts as ‘without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history’ in email to staff

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Canva is cutting or relocating more than 1,200 jobs, representing 22% of its global workforce, as part of a major restructure that includes laying off staff who helped build the Australian-founded design platform.
The changes mirror a trend across the technology sector, where software companies are fighting to stay competitive against cheaper artificial intelligence disrupters while aggressively embedding AI tools themselves.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canva layoffs: design giant to cut or relocate more than 1,200 jobs in major restructure

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Report says cost of maintenance could soon reach £2m a week, including 24-hour patrols to avert fire risk
The Palace of Westminster will be at risk of a Notre Dame-style fire or a similar catastrophic event if MPs do not tackle the issue of funding refurbishments, a parliamentary committee has said.
Decisions about how and when to begin a full restoration of the building, which is Grade I-listed and a Unesco world heritage site, have been repeatedly delayed amid disagreement over how it should be done and spiralling costs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Houses of Parliament at risk of ‘Notre Dame-style fire’ as renovation costs rise

articles.author: Natricia Duncan in St John's
articles.description:
Speaking in Antigua, the king did not give explicit support for reparations but said he wanted to ‘address past wrongs’
King Charles has said that deepening his understanding of the horrors of slavery has made him more determined to address the wrongs of the past, as Caribbean leaders and campaigners intensified demands for an apology and reparations from Britain.
“We cannot change the actions of those who came before us,” Charles told leaders at the opening of the Commonwealth summit in Antigua and Barbuda on Tuesday. “We can, however, learn from the past.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: King Charles addresses summit as demands for slavery apology grow

articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
articles.description:
The incident took place in the same province where a grizzly attacked a group of schoolchildren last November
A mother is dead and her daughter is missing in western Canada after a suspected grizzly bear attack in the same community where a bear attacked a group of schoolchildren earlier in the year.
On Tuesday, the British Columbia conservation officer service said in a social media post that it had launched a search for the two missing people on the weekend, and that during the search on Sunday an officer found the mother’s body. The search for her 19-year-old daughter is ongoing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One dead and another missing in suspected grizzly bear attack in Canada

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
George Madgwick, party leader on Hampshire county council, faces charges related to four teenagers between 2008 and 2021
Reform UK’s leader on Hampshire county council has been charged with 12 counts of rape and one of distributing indecent images of a child.
George Madgwick, 37, who is a councillor in Portsmouth and leads the Reform group on the council, was a prominent voice linked to recent protests in the city connected to the arrival of asylum seekers on small boats.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reform UK councillor charged with 12 counts of rape and multiple other offences

articles.author: AFP in Madrid
articles.description:
Óscar Puente also announces his withdrawal from upcoming election following disaster that killed 69 people
Spain’s transport minister handed in his resignation on Tuesday after the train crash that killed 69 people last week, one of the worst railway disasters in Europe this century.
Óscar Puente, who had earlier pledged to work “tirelessly” to restore confidence in the world’s second-largest high-speed rail network, also said he was withdrawing from the country’s upcoming general election.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Spanish transport minister resigns after deadly train crash

articles.author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
articles.description:
Nobel winner warns the tech could be near to triggering major incident such as power or banking shutdown
One of the “godfathers of AI”, Geoffrey Hinton, has said it could turn out that humans would have been better off never developing the technology as he warned it could trigger a large-scale incident this year or next, such as a temporary blackout of financial or power systems.
The Nobel prize-winning computer scientist told the Guardian he is not a “doomer” about the technology that is underpinned by his groundbreaking research into artificial neural networks and believes AI has the potential to lead to a “wonderful future” but he said “it might be that we would have been better off never developing it”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI ‘godfather’ Geoffrey Hinton: it might turn out we were better off without AI

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Akande joining the international court of justice comes a decade after previous British judge failed to get re-elected
A British judge has been elected on to the UN’s international court of justice, in a big British diplomatic victory that comes almost 10 years after a previous British judge failed to get re-elected.
Dapo Akande will now serve as one of the ICJ’s 15 judges for a minimum nine-year term.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British lawyer Dapo Akande elected to UN top court in big diplomatic win

articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now) and Jakub Krupa (earlier)
articles.description:
Bomb threats were made on routes involving a number of airlines, including Ryanair and WizzAir
Back to Poland, Warsaw Modlin airport says it has resumed operations after an earlier bomb threat – but a part of the airport where the London flight was parked remain closed and is being checked by security forces.
Ukraine’s Zelenskyy has said his talks with Merz and Germany’s president Steinmeier will focus on “diplomatic coordination” on air defence and energy sector.
“These will be the priorities of today’s talks. We all have an interest in security, stability, and protecting the rules-based international order. And we must work together to turn these principles into concrete decisions and actions.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Seven reported bomb threats against European flights confirmed as false alarms – as it happened

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh, Gwyn Topham and Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Unclear if series of incidents affecting two UK departures and several Ryanair services, among others, were connected
Seven planes across Europe have been searched or diverted after a series of bomb threats were made to passenger flights, prompting questions as to whether there was any coordination behind the warnings.
Two UK departures – one from Heathrow and one from Manchester – were among those threatened in what Downing Street called “malicious hoaxes”, though all planes landed safely and no explosives were found.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Seven planes across Europe searched or diverted after ‘malicious hoax’ bomb threats

articles.author: Andrew Roth
articles.description:
US president makes surprise election day announcement, saying country does not ‘need’ $4bn annual payment
Donald Trump has said that the US will end military aid to Israel at the end of this year in a surprise election day announcement that appeared to be targeted at voters sceptical of US support for Israel and the war in Gaza.
In a phone interview with Fox News as voting began on Tuesday morning, the US president said the US would cut nearly $4bn (£2.96bn) in military aid to Israel because “they don’t need it”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump claims US will end military aid to Israel by end of this year

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
A previously unseen family archive offers a glimpse into the Indian Nobel prize winner’s artistic process and personal relationships in his final years

Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

It’s easy to run out of words to describe Rabindranath Tagore. The first non-European to win the Nobel prize in literature, Tagore was a Bengali poet, musician, novelist, philosopher, songwriter, painter, humanist and educator.
Born in 1861, Tagore left an indelible mark on the subcontinent’s literature, music, education and art. Among his enduring legacies are the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The private creative world of Rabindranath Tagore, the man Yeats called ‘greater than any of us’

articles.author: Patrick Wintour and Jonathan Yerushalmy
articles.description:
Strikes on eve of US midterms reportedly target surface-to-air missiles being used against US assets
The ⁠US launched limited strikes on ​Iran’s Qeshm Island late on Monday, hours after the vice-president, JD Vance, said he was optimistic that diplomatic efforts to end the war were moving in the right direction.
The strikes, disclosed by Iranians on social media and confirmed by US Central Command (Centcom), came on the eve of crucial midterm elections in which Donald Trump’s Republican party is expected to be punished by voters. Diplomatic mediators believe it will be clear within two days whether the basis for continued indirect talks between the US and Iran exists.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island as Vance voices optimism about a deal

articles.author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
articles.description:
Beijing launches diplomatic salvo to woo Gulf leaders and bolster its influence in the region
China has held a flurry of meetings with Gulf leaders in a sign that Beijing is stepping up its diplomatic efforts in the Middle East.
The diplomatic salvo comes before a highly anticipated meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping when the US president is expected to attend the Apec conference in Shenzhen, China, on 18 and 19 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s troubles with Iran could open the door to China

articles.author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
articles.description:
Cop30 host sets out steps to break link with coal, oil and gas as it aims to move focus from negotiating to implementing
All countries can start to break their dependence on fossil fuels now without needing to wait for new technologies or economic changes, Brazil’s government has said ahead of a global climate summit.
Brazil, the host of last year’s UN climate conference, set out the world’s first global “roadmap” for phasing out fossil fuels on Tuesday, showing that countries could boost their economies and pull people out of poverty while breaking the link with coal, oil and gas.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil publishes first global ‘roadmap’ for phasing out fossil fuels

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield, Elisângela Mendonça and Phoebe Weston and Spoorthy Raman
articles.description:
Guardian and Mongabay reveal approaches to officials and MPs on behalf of  Vantara zoo ahead of UK-chaired Cites meeting on endangered animal imports

British government ministers were told not to engage formally with Vantara, the controversial mega-zoo run by the Indian billionaire Anant Ambani, after lobbying efforts by the private animal sanctuary in the run-up to a UK-chaired meeting on the trade in endangered species, according to documents.
This week, the UK heads a 32-country committee meeting in Geneva of Cites, the United Nations body that regulates trade in endangered species. The meeting will examine how India has responded to compliance concerns about imports of endangered animals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK ministers told not to engage formally with Indian mega-zoo after lobbying

articles.author: Ian Sample Science editor
articles.description:
Chemical tests on Aratasaurus bone identify presence of heme, the organic compound that allows haemoglobin in blood to carry oxygen around body
It could be the opening of a Jurassic Park rip-off: scientists examining ancient dinosaur bones find what appear to be fossilised red blood cells, and traces of the molecule that gives the beast’s blood its distinctive crimson hue.
But that is what researchers are claiming to have discovered after analysing the hind leg bones of a small, meat-eating dinosaur called an Aratasaurus that lived and died in what is now north-eastern Brazil 115m years ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fossilised red blood cells found in 115m-year-old dinosaur’s bone, say scientists

articles.author: Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
Brent crude drops by more than 6% to $105.55 a barrel, the lowest level in more than two weeks
The oil price has fallen to its lowest level in more two weeks amid new hopes of a breakthrough to end the Iran war.
Brent crude, the international benchmark, dropped by more than 6.5% to as low as $105.55 a barrel on Monday, the lowest since 16 October, sending shares in airline companies higher and pushing down government borrowing costs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Oil price falls amid hope of a breakthrough to end Iran war

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Survey finds UK government’s decision to impose trade ban was not a decisive factor in how Israelis voted in election
The UK government’s decision to impose a ban on trade in goods from illegal settlements was not decisive in how Israelis voted in their general election, but a majority think the Israeli government’s settlements policy should change if it is going to lead to further sanctions, a new poll of Israelis shows.
There had been fierce criticism of the UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband’s decision in September to impose a trade ban and wider sanctions on illegal settlements, with some claiming it would drive Israeli voters into the arms of Benjamin Netanyahu.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Most Israelis think settlements policy should change to avoid more sanctions, poll finds

articles.author: Julian Borger in Umm al-Fahm
articles.description:
Yousef Jabareen says he is ready to join forces with opposition bloc to oust Benjamin Netanyahu after winning record number of seats in Knesset
The leader of Israel’s main Palestinian coalition, which holds the balance of power after Tuesday’s elections, has said the country is facing a historic opportunity to change direction.
Yousef Jabareen, the head of the Joint List, said he was ready to join forces with the “Change” bloc to oust Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right coalition, and to wrest control of the Knesset.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israel has ‘historic’ opportunity to change direction, says leader of Arab coalition

articles.author: Natricia Duncan in St John's, Antigua
articles.description:
British prime minister has now agreed to structured dialogue on reparatory justice but issue remains off formal Chogm agenda 
British officials reportedly insisted that discussions of reparations for slavery should not be on the agenda of the Commonwealth leaders’ summit in Antigua and Barbuda – and even warned that Andy Burnham would not attend the meeting if the subject was formally included, according to a leading Caribbean political figure.
Ralph Gonsalves, a former prime minister of St Vincent and the Grenadines and a senior figure in the reparatory justice movement Repair Campaign, welcomed Britain’s decision to enter structured dialogue on reparations, but said the UK had come “kicking and screaming” to the conversation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK was ‘vehement’ slavery reparations should not be on Commonwealth summit agenda

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Led by Congress party, India’s opposition alliance channels anger over removal of 130 million names from voter roll
Thousands of opposition supporters have gathered in Delhi as protests against the Narendra Modi government continue to gather momentum.
Led by the Congress party, India’s opposition alliance has brought together supporters from across the country, amid growing anger over a large-scale revision of the country’s voter roll that has seen 130 million names erased.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tens of thousands protest against Narendra Modi regime in Delhi

articles.author: Eduardo Porter
articles.description:
A truce has cooled the trade conflict, but neither country has done anything to limit the outbreak of new hostilities
Donald Trump’s trade wars have largely fallen off the headlines. Fears of new tariffs flare up from time to time when the US president goes off the rails – for instance, threatening to end US trade with countries with which it has a deficit unless the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates. But the sense that the world’s two largest economies are plowing ahead into an overt economic conflagration has taken a back seat to other, more salient fears, about Trump ending American democracy, AI killing us all and stuff like that.
The sense of calm is misleading. Under the radar, the world is marching toward an economic war of potentially epic proportions, one that, history suggests, could well spill over into the real thing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The US-China trade war seems to have subsided – but the sense of calm is misleading

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Cryptocurrency exchange says 90% of losses covered as FBI blames North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor

The cryptocurrency exchange Binance has started to allow its customers to withdraw their funds from the platform, as it recovers from a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack.
The exchange was hit by the theft on Thursday, which has since been described as the biggest heist in history, with experts identifying North Korea as the likely culprit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Binance resumes customer withdrawals after record $6.3bn hack

articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
articles.description:
Alliance for the Future, unveiled at Montreal summit and open to other countries, conceived for world ‘shaken by new storms’
Canada and Europe have announced a new alliance of like-minded nations to serve as both a “protective canopy under which our citizens can thrive” and a powerful hedge against the unpredictable nature of geopolitics, while welcoming other countries to join.
Speaking to reporters on Friday from Montreal, the prime minister, Mark Carney, and the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, called the new partnership the Alliance for the Future and said the “deepest possible partnership between Canada and the 27-member bloc had the potential to offer unprecedented stability and opportunity”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada and EU announce new alliance open to like-minded countries

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Cryptocurrency theft is estimated to generate half of the country’s foreign currency income
North Korea plays by its own rules. The isolated, secretive and autocratic country is largely cut off from the world’s economic system – but when it comes to generating foreign earnings it relies on some of the world’s most sophisticated hacking.
Experts, such as TRM Labs, quickly attributed the extraordinary $6.3bn (£4.7bn) Binance cryptocurrency theft to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit that has also been known as the Lazarus Group. Though the link may not be proven yet, the pattern of behaviour is familiar.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How crypto hacking funds isolated North Korea’s nuclear programme

articles.author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
articles.description:
Forums for discussion of feminist and LGBTQ+ views face growing intolerance from Chinese state, say experts
Beijing’s annual independent queer film festival has been cancelled after what is understood to have been a campaign of sustained harassment from authorities.
Beijing Queer film festival, which was due to begin on Friday in China’s capital, is one of the country’s oldest independent film festivals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Beijing Queer film festival cancelled after harassment from authorities

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Durban Deep
articles.description:
There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective
Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991. But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area.
In late September, dozens of zama zamas – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa, meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sinkholes, scarred land and scapegoats: the scourge of illegal gold mining in Johannesburg

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi
articles.description:
Critics cite Lana Nusseibeh’s denial of accusations the UAE is fuelling Sudan war by supporting paramilitary RSF
Members of the Sudanese diaspora and international human rights monitors have denounced the candidature of an Emirati diplomat for the top job at the UN, citing her denial of accusations that the United Arab Emirates is fuelling the war in Sudan by supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.
The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become gridlocked.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sudanese diaspora and human rights groups denounce UAE nominee for UN top job

articles.author: Peter Beaumont
articles.description:
Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website
Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country.
Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Egypt fines prominent editor Lina Attalah and shuts independent news outlet Mada Masr

articles.author: Sarah Johnson
articles.description:
Jean Kaseya, of the Africa CDC, warns of the illness spreading like Covid unless more funding is secured to increase preparedness and possible treatment
The “unprecedented” spread of the Ebola outbreak means it could reach the UK and other countries, according to one of Africa’s top health officials.
As the current outbreak reached 10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths, Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic, which first took hold in China before spreading to countries across the world, claiming millions of lives, and ravaging health systems and economies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Africa’s ‘unprecedented’ Ebola outbreak could reach UK, says top health official

articles.description:

articles.description:
It will take decades to rebuild trust in a country that removed a tyrant once – and then reinstated him four years later
When Joe Biden entered the White House in 2021 it was possible to believe that Donald Trump’s reign had been an aberration. “America is back. The transatlantic alliance is back,” the new president declared to relieved European leaders shortly after winning the 2020 race. It was true, but not for long.
Trump’s defeat proved that US democracy was mechanically operational, not culturally robust. His supporters tried violent subversion to prevent the inauguration of a successor. A second term should have been unthinkable. Republicans who failed to denounce the 6 January insurrection should have been unelectable. Instead, within four years, US voters reinstated the champion of a failed coup against their cherished constitution as commander-in-chief.
Rafael Behr is a Guardian columnist

The Athenian led the people, he didn’t follow them, writes Prof Costas Milas
Your editorial (The Guardian view on a changing Brexit debate: Kemi Badenoch is trapped in denial, 29 October) notes that when it comes to Brexit, Andy Burnham appears to be following the voters. This, in my humble opinion, is a problem. Thucydides noted about Pericles, the Athenian statesman, that “it was he who led them [the people], rather than they who led him”.
It was arguably the constant and thoughtful guidance of Pericles to his fellow Athenian citizens that made Athens the dominant political and economic power, respected by its friends and enemies alike. Burnham needs to take the lead and show his cards on what type of relationship he wants to pursue with our European partners. All those mindless automatons queueing up to use your bus, bar or bed store, or whatever workplace you are trapped in for the duration of the game. The endless repetitive tasks. The emptiness of the world beyond your corporate existence. Together, these elements scream existential terror … which is perhaps why we are now seeing a new indie sub-genre of job sim horror games, including Home Safety Hotline, Dredge and more recently, Grease Trap ’99, a Lovecraftian mystery set in a Scottish chip shop.
Now, we have Night Plane, in which you take on the role of a flight attendant on a jumbo jet to hell. It all starts kind of normally. You turn up for the first day of your new job, meet your colleagues, then take your spot at the departure gate, checking in customers and being careful to root out anyone with invalid tickets. If your social media algorithms have clocked that you’re into video games, something strange will have happened in the past few weeks. Your feed, like mine, will have been full of clips of streamers playing bizarre mashups of popular video games. Skyrim in Minecraft. Halo, except the main character is Mario. Skate 2 in Call of Duty maps. A flood of professional-looking fan-coded game mods that are mildly interesting to look at for 30 seconds, but ultimately inconsequential. Would I download a mod that lets me play Wii Bowling inside a zombie shooter? No, but I am very interested in where they came from.
Of course, the answer – or at least, most of the answer – is AI. After a week of researching this (thanks especially to Replay Mode on YouTube for this informative video, which set me down this track) I now understand that these mashup mods are not just AI-generated videos, but AI-assisted coding. Basically, as of a few weeks ago, Anthropic’s Claude has become extremely good at decompiling video game code. Games are written by humans in readable code and then compiled into binary 1s and 0s that the PC or console running it can read; decompiling is the reversal of that process, revealing a game’s source code, which humans can then edit and mess around with for fun. This used to be an extremely laborious process. But now it is not, because humans aren’t doing much of it any more.

“Only a crisis – actual or perceived – produces real change. When that crisis occurs, the actions that are taken depend on the ideas that are lying around,” he wrote. The job of intellectuals, thinktanks and economists, he argued, is to refine the quality of these ambient ideas, so that good ones are ready when disaster strikes.

Autonomous cars, which may be the safest we have built, keep getting easily avoidable parking tickets. That is the state of AI today: impressively capable at something complex, yet embarrassingly clumsy at something easy. And it has implications for what work will remain human and what will be automated by AI.

articles.description:
Wikipedia’s 68m articles have been consulted trillions of times. Not bad for a website that has barely changed since it was founded 20 years ago
A few years ago, I was struck by the tension between how Wikipedia was used, and how it was talked about. Everyone was on it all the time, and yet its reputation had stalled at “don’t trust it”, because it was the “free encyclopedia that anyone can edit”.
Clearly people were trusting it, so much so it had become part of the fabric of everyday life since it was founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001. But despite the fact it now has been consulted trillions of times by billions of people (English Wikipedia alone is 5.2bn words long), it inspires an odd lack of curiosity. Even people donating to Wikipedia might say the money was “for the factcheckers”, though there aren’t any – not paid ones, anyway. Meanwhile, the internet in the social media era had begun to feel like a much uglier place, and some digital nostalgia was setting in: here was this holdover that had somehow survived; a website that functions – and even looks – much the same as it did 20 years ago.
